subject: Residency exit playbook request — evidence & logistics
messages:
From: Lisa Huang <lisa@medicorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency exit playbook request — what evidence we’ll need

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our Private deployment onboarding review we need a clear playbook and list of artifacts we should expect if we ever do a tenant exit / data handback from Redwood in our VPC deployment. Specifically Medicorp needs:

- Concrete artifact types you can provide (disk snapshot manifests, object listings, retention logs, audit logs, snapshot hashes, encryption key state)
- A clear timeline for handback (when the snapshot is taken, how long verification takes, expected completion window)
- KMS/key management details — do you perform key deletion on our behalf or provide tombstone evidence we can perform locally?
- Proof that no replicas remain in other regions (we need a short attestation we can keep in procurement file)

Can you also confirm typical SLAs for completing an exit (we may have contractual language to propose)? Procurement copied.

Attachments: [Attachment: medicorp-exit-questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

Appreciate a short response and a proposed call time this week.

Best,
Lisa Huang\Senior Security Program Manager\MediCorp Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@medicorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency exit playbook request — what evidence we’ll need

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. High level answers here and I’ve attached our checklist template so you can see the artifacts and a sample timeline.

Short answers:
- Artifacts we can deliver:
  * Snapshot manifest CSV (object path, size, sha256),
  * Access-controlled object export (S3-compatible manifest + signed URLs for pick-up),
  * Audit log bundle (API access, deletion events),
  * Snapshot hash receipts and notarized manifest (PDF),
  * Region replication map (which AZ/region replicas existed during snapshot).
- Timeline: typical delivery window is 7–21 business days depending on snapshot size and whether there is a custom export format. Small tenants (<=2TB) usually complete in 7–10 business days; multi-region replication or large exports may run to 3 weeks.
- Keys: for Private/VPC deployments we support two models: customer-managed KMS (preferred) where you control key deletion; or provider-managed envelope keys where we can produce a signed key-derivation/tombstone certificate and an attestation that keys were destroyed per procedure. We will not force deletion of a customer-managed KMS key.
- Replicas: we provide an attestation listing known replica locations at the time of final snapshot and the actions taken to remove replicas.

I’m attaching: residency-exit-checklist-v1.docx (our standard checklist) and erase-evidence-template.xlsx (evidence matrix you can share with your legal/procurement).

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thu 9/9 at 10:00am PT? If that works I’ll loop in Karthik (for technical runbook) and Ben (security attestation).

Attachments: [Attachment: residency-exit-checklist-v1.docx (DOCX)], [Attachment: erase-evidence-template.xlsx (XLSX)]

Thanks,
Marissa Cole\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference\m: (415) 555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Residency exit playbook request — internal next steps

Internal — forwarding Medicorp thread. Action items:

- Karthik: draft the technical runbook (export steps, snapshot commands, storage path mapping, verification hash generation). Ensure it covers both customer-managed KMS and provider-managed envelope key flows. Target: initial draft by 9/9 EOD.
- Ben: prepare the security attestation template and list of logs we can produce (audit bundle format, retention ranges). Please validate that our standard attestation language meets SOC2 evidence needs — we may need legal tweaks.
- Olga: once Ben drafts attestation, please review for procurement language and any constraints re: certificate notarization (we have a DocuSign flow for signed attestations; confirm).

Notes: Medicorp called out needing confirmation we can provide a region-replica map and a signed manifest. For large tenants we should plan for an incremental snapshot approach to avoid long export windows.

Marissa
From: Lisa Huang <lisa@medicorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicorp.com
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency exit playbook request — what evidence we’ll need

Marissa,

Thanks — Thu 9/9 10:00am PT works for us; invite received. Procurement attached a target timeline so you can see contractual milestones. A couple quick clarifications before the call:

1) For customer-managed KMS, we just need a written statement that Redwood will not delete or rotate the key without explicit Medicorp authorization. Can you confirm that in writing?
2) For provider-managed keys: is the attestation you provide sufficient for us to mark the data as unrecoverable in our compliance artifacts (i.e., can we rely on that attestation to satisfy auditors)?

Attached: [Attachment: medicorp-procurement-timeline.xlsx (XLSX)]

Short answer on (1): yes, we will not delete a customer-managed KMS key without documented customer authorization; we will provide a written statement for your procurement file.

On (2): our attestation is intended to be relied on by customers and auditors; Ben will bring the exact wording on the call. If your auditors require notarization or an independent third-party verification, we can discuss options (e.g., signed attestation + optional third-party witness).

Look forward to the call.

Best,
Lisa
